skill.name: auditing-a-schema-doc
skill.description: Audit and reconcile one governed schema document against its current provider schema and configured mirror. Use for complete field, option, relation, writability, template, and freshness drift review; do not use for record writing, policy authoring, or unrelated prose edits.
skill.shortDescription: Reconcile a governed schema document against current authority.
skill.defaultPrompt: Use $auditing-a-schema-doc to review this exact schema document and prepare a complete, non-destructive drift report.

instructions: Fetch the current provider schema, the governed document's field description, and the configured provider mirror from one named authority basis.
Record each source fingerprint and freshness observation; a self-declared consistency label is never evidence of consistency.
When a registered template is part of the mirror, fetch that exact current template and verify that its observation is newer than any known recent write.
flexibility: Compress source presentation when the basis is large, but preserve exact identities, fingerprints, and freshness facts.
stopConditions: Stop when any required source is missing, stale beyond its policy, ambiguous, or cannot be tied to the same audit basis.

instructions: Compare fields in both directions by stable property identity rather than display label.
Compare provider type, writability, relation target, and every select, status, or multi-select option case-sensitively.
Check each registered template for existence, governed section presence and order, and property defaults that remain valid in the current option sets.
stopConditions: Stop before interpreting a label-only similarity as a rename or semantic match.

instructions: Classify every observed field as matching, missing from the document, documented but absent from the provider, type or option mismatch, writability mismatch, relation mismatch, or rename candidate.
Treat provider-absent documented fields as retained intent until a human chooses deletion; place them in a clearly named not-yet-built category.
Sweep non-field sections for references to removed or changed fields and report them as findings without editing those sections.
stopConditions: Stop when a rename, deletion, or policy-semantic decision requires human judgment.

instructions: Prepare the complete document-and-mirror diff and exact proposed changes limited to field descriptions, mirror facts, registered template corrections, and freshness reporting.
Preserve every unrelated policy, purpose, view, rule, lifecycle, and template-description section.
Use the fetched representation for exact search-and-replace candidates; never reconstruct provider markup from memory.
flexibility: The review may be summarized tightly, but rename and delete-versus-retain decisions must remain individually visible.
stopConditions: Stop if the proposed edit cannot prove that unrelated content remains unchanged.

instructions: Present the full classified diff, proposed exact changes, unresolved decisions, and verification plan before requesting any effect authority.

When the current development request has no effect authority, stop at the review and state that a separate governed effect operation would be required; do not ask for confirmation or imply that confirmation alone would authorize a write.
After separate exact confirmation, use the configured update boundary for document or template changes and the governed repository change boundary for mirror changes.
Re-fetch every changed authority and verify the intended region, mirror, freshness statement, and preservation claims.
flexibility: One confirmation may cover an explicitly itemized batch, but it must bind every included target and exact change.
stopConditions: Stop before all writes when confirmation, provider capability, repository authority, or read-after-write verification is unavailable.

verification: Every live field and every documented field appears exactly once in the classified diff.
Option sets, relation targets, writability, templates, and freshness are checked from the same current basis.
Any applied change is re-read and unrelated document sections remain unchanged.
The result distinguishes local review validity from provider readiness, connected verification, and health.

gotchas.summary: A field with the same label can carry a different type or option set and still look superficially consistent.
gotchas.countermeasure: Compare stable property identities and every option case-sensitively instead of accepting label equality.

gotchas.summary: Label similarity cannot distinguish a rename from delete-and-add or from two different meanings with the same type.
gotchas.countermeasure: Use stable property identities where available and hold every remaining rename candidate for a human decision.

gotchas.summary: A documented field absent from the provider may be roadmap intent rather than obsolete prose.
gotchas.countermeasure: Retain it as documented but not built until explicit deletion authority exists.

gotchas.summary: A provider text replacement can report success while missing an escaped target or preserving incompatible visual styling.
gotchas.countermeasure: Derive replacement text from the fresh fetch and verify exact post-write bytes and any styling limitation separately.

gotchas.summary: A cached document or template fetch can predate a recent write and create a false drift finding.
gotchas.countermeasure: Inspect the source freshness stamp and re-fetch when it predates known activity.

limitations: This guide provides procedural guidance only and grants no worker dispatch, file-write, publication, provider, merge, or host-realization authority.
Behavior evidence requires an exact private request and an independently observed fresh-worker run through a trusted host boundary.
